title: Pigeonhole → Averages: the pigeonhole principle and the extremal principle of averages
summary: One argument at three levels of abstraction: a fixed global total forces a local extreme. Try to beat the pigeonhole principle and meet the counting obstruction, then the generalised principle (some box holds at least ⌈N/k⌉, some at most ⌊N/k⌋) with the balanced configuration and a threshold line, contradiction proofs that push every bar below or above the average, and the integer bars turning into real heights so that min ≤ mean ≤ max. Liquid equalisation, deviations summing to zero, equality and strictness, four proof modes, a theorem constructor, minimax balancing, seven worked examples (socks, birth months, exam scores, workload, graph degrees, dragged distances, and continuous time as a continuous analogue), weighted averages, centre of mass and convex combinations, a convex-hull teaser, challenges, a free-play lab with a lock-total mode, a concept map, a Cmd/Ctrl+K palette and a final synthesis animation. Deterministic, offline, with a narrated beamdswitch deck.
